overview: Rise 6.1.30's NoFall is a ModeValue shell with twelve modes, default Spoof, all orbiting the shared FallDistanceComponent: at very low priority the component accumulates lastTickPosY minus posY into a static float on every PreMotion and resets it to zero when the event claims onGround, and the modes read and rewrite that accumulator to hide fall distance from the client's damage code and to shape the C03 flag. Spoof, the default, forces event.setOnGround(true) every tick with no packet of its own. The packet modes send a bare C03PacketPlayer(true) (Packet, VulcanAndVerus with a 0.5 timer, Watchdog's LessFall), a C06 poslook with onGround true (Place with a trailing C08 use-item, Flag's teleport response), a 1.5-block y drop (Invalid), a 0.098 sink with motionY zeroed (ChunkLoad), a rounded-ground claim (Round), a sub-pixel jitter with onGround false (NoGround), a strafe slowdown plus flag claim (Matrix), a blink freeze (Watchdog), and a water-bucket clutch (Clutch).

sections.p: FallDistanceComponent is the module's state: it adds the per-tick vertical drop to a static float, resets on an onGround claim, and runs at very low priority so every mode can rewrite the value afterwards. All twelve modes hook PreMotionEvent (Clutch uses PreUpdateEvent) and most follow the same shape: read the distance, and when it exceeds 3.0 (the vanilla damage threshold is 3.0), apply the mode's spoof and zero the accumulator. The component's distance is fully client-side: it is the field the modes fake, while the vanilla fallDistance field on the player object is what the client's own damage code reads, and the modes never need to touch it because the flag spoof resets the server-side counter instead.

Spoof claims onGround true on every tick; Round snaps the position to roundToGround when the distance exceeds 3 and the rounded y is within 0.005 of the event y, claiming the snapped ground; NoGround claims onGround false with a 1e-20 jitter; Matrix, gated on a block under the player, strafes at 0.19 above distance 2 and claims onGround true with speed below 0.2 past distance 3. The packet modes emit their own C03s: Packet sends a bare C03PacketPlayer(true), Place sends a C06 poslook with onGround true followed by a C08 use-item, Flag corrupts the accumulator to -999 with a random y lift past 3 and answers every teleport with a C06 claiming ground, Invalid drops the event y by 1.5 when the block below the predicted position is solid, and VulcanAndVerus pairs the C03(true) with a 0.5 timer-speed cut to smooth the server-side fall.

WatchdogNoFall is a blink-based mode: when the player is one tick off ground with downward motion and a block below but nothing within 3 blocks, it arms the start flag and every subsequent PreMotion calls PingSpoofComponent.spoof(99999, true, false, false, false, true), buffering the movement stream while claiming onGround true, until the player lands and dispatch() replays the buffer; its LessFall toggle is the plain C03(true) plus 0.5-timer path. ChunkLoadNoFall fakes a chunk unload below the player: past distance 3 with a solid block ahead it zeroes the distance and sets fakeUnloaded, and while that flag is set it zeroes motionY, claims onGround false, sinks 0.098 per tick and calls setPositionAndUpdate, until a TeleportEvent clears the flag. ClutchNoFall is the legitimate half: past fallDistance 2 with a block under within 15 blocks it finds a water bucket, rotates to the nearest solid block via RotationComponent and right-clicks to place water, a real clutch that needs no spoof.

files.label: NoFall.java
files.explanation: The dispatcher registers twelve modes and defaults to Spoof, with no logic of its own. The mode list matters because the countering set splits by mechanism: flag-only modes (Spoof, NoGround, Round, Matrix) are caught by ground-truth checks, packet modes (Packet, Place, Flag, Invalid, VulcanAndVerus) by the same ground-truth checks plus rate and envelope checks, and the blink mode (Watchdog) by the blink countering set.

files.label: FallDistanceComponent.java
files.explanation: The component is the shared accumulator every mode reads and rewrites: it adds lastTickPosY minus posY to a static float on each PreMotion at very low priority and resets it to zero whenever the event claims onGround. Modes zero it after spoofing, so the client's own damage code never sees a fall past the threshold while the module is active, and the component's distance is also the gate for the velocity-aware modes (Vulcan, Watchdog criticals gate on the same component). This file is what makes the twelve modes a single coherent module instead of twelve independent hacks.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (block-cache ground truth)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly never trusts the packet flag: fromOnGround and toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround() scanning the block cache at minY minus the yOnGround epsilon, the vertical allowance is vDistRel seeded by momentum, and the violation (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 reverts the move with a set-back. A Spoof-style onGround true claim over open air does nothing to the envelope, because the trace says the position is not grounded, and the packet modes that carry position changes (Round's snapped ground, Invalid's 1.5-block drop, ChunkLoad's 0.098-per-tick sink) each present vertical deltas the momentum model rejects. The honest bypass surface is the sub-0.03 offsets: NoGround's 1e-20 jitter and any sub-pixel claim shift y by less than the min-move, so the envelope never sees them, and flag-only claims with no position change are invisible to it entirely.

countering.label: NoFall (server-side fall ledger)
countering.explanation: Vrekt keeps its own fall accounting: MovingListener records the last grounded location and its physics-derived ground state while PacketListener stores the raw packet flag, and the check fires when the vertical distance from the last grounded location reaches 3.0, the player is descending, Vrekt's ground state is airborne and the client claimed onGround while the server fall distance is zero, raising "Fall distance is 0 while not onGround. (Client faked)" and damaging the player on cancel. Every Rise flag-claim mode hits this the moment it claims ground 3 or more blocks below the last grounded spot while descending, which is exactly the Spoof and Round posture. The tolerance is the design gap: claims within a 3-block descent and genuine landings pass, so the working bypass is to claim ground only when a real block is actually below, which is what the block-gated modes (Matrix, ChunkLoad) approximate and why the check still catches their y-bearing variants.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (lag-compensated trace)
countering.explanation: Hawk compares the claimed flag against a server-side solid trace: for position updates it uses the lag-compensated event ground state, otherwise it traces AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally at the predicted position with a 0.001 velocity tolerance, and on a mismatch it re-tests the pre-move position at the clipped y, skips step and web cases, then punishes and rubber-bands. With the preventNoFall setting it rewrites the raw packet bytes to force onGround false on the wire, so even a successful claim is corrected server-side. The module's block-gated modes (Matrix, ChunkLoad) are the honest threat to this check: they only claim ground when a solid block is predicted below, which keeps the trace honest, while the unconditional claimers (Spoof, Round, Flag) fail the trace every tick. Claims within 0.02 of real terrain pass by design.

countering.label: NoFall (post-prediction flag check)
countering.explanation: Grim's NoFall runs after prediction on PLAYER_FLYING and PLAYER_ROTATION and only examines flag-only claims: an onGround true with no position change builds a 0.6 by 0.001 feet box at the simulated position, expands it by the movement threshold, and collides against the compensated world plus hard entities; no collision flags with a 10-tick setback and rewrites the flag to false when modification is allowed. The Spoof default is a direct hit: it claims onGround true on every tick with no position change while airborne, and the collision finds nothing below. Position-bearing spoofs are skipped by design and routed to the prediction-based GroundSpoof check instead, and claims within about 0.6 of terrain pass, which is the tolerance band the block-gated modes can exploit by claiming only near real ground.
